items.title: An Endless Flight
items.summary: A ship skims an endless world that changes as it flies: open sea under red cliffs, plains, forests and mountains, mirrored in the water, all generated on your device from a seed and driven through MCP.

Then shape it by name with the parameters listed in describe.infinite.params - oceans, rocky, water_reflect, boost, sparks - and add {op:'lens', on:true} for the sun. Use the linked scene as a starting point.

items.prompt:
In Polynite, compose a detailed Japanese pagoda from nested assemblies. Define a bracket group, repeat it in a frontage, repeat the frontage around a storey, then repeat uniformly scaled storeys with taper. Use shared swept roof panels and ribs, procedural vermilion wood, dark tiles, warm paper and gold fittings. Keep storey count, width, taper, eave lift and detail switches editable. Treat this recipe as a starting point: invent other structures using the same operators. Estimate before applying, inspect bounds and observe the rendered result. Preserve the current scene.

Reference: https://explore.polynite.io/docs/recipes/nested-temple/

Disable roof ribs to compare detail; save your independent scene.
steps: Define reusable mesh prototypes and local bracket/frontage/storey assembly definitions.
Compose bounded assembly calls with local translation, yaw, uniform scale and repeat.
Apply procedural material roles, inspect the flattened plan and actual GPU sharing, then observe and save.
items.settings: Open & test > Variant or Adjust. In Polynite: Scene settings > Living architecture > temple > layout/shape. All assembly definitions and material choices are in the downloadable recipe JSON.
items.limits: Realtime parametric study inspired by the proportions and layered detail of Golden Temple. items.title: Give every object room
items.summary: An object moves to the first free candidate when a neighbouring construction grows. Named reservations, complete-object radius and clearance remain editable recipe data.
items.prompt:
In the current Polynite scene, compose editable placement recipes using named footprint reservations. Discover commands.recipe_footprints and operators footprint/context/spatial/let. Declare conservative roof, canopy and access rectangles, bind only explicit nearby sources, and preserve a whole-object radius plus clearance margin. Try a preferred position and four bounded alternatives; reject atomically if none fits. Add explicit pair constraints between placed objects. Keep geometry, aesthetic choices and candidate rules in JSON recipes; reuse existing geometry and terrain operators. Estimate, apply with stable IDs, inspect bounds and actual pixels. Preserve user edits and locks; do not clear the current scene.

Reference: https://explore.polynite.io/docs/recipes/footprint-placement/
try: Press Play: the construction widens, the nearby object changes position, then both return.
Under Adjust, change place x, z, search, radius or margin. Keep radius large enough for the complete object.
Grow source width. If all five candidates are blocked, move the preferred point or widen search.
steps: Publish named horizontal reservations as footprint nodes, without duplicate render geometry.
Measure each candidate against explicit sources; preserve the complete-object radius plus margin, then choose the first free candidate.
Attach reused objects to the chosen terrain-seated anchor; validate spacing pairs and keep all rules in editable recipe data.
items.settings: Adjust > place · recipe controls: x, z, search, radius, margin. source > width changes its reservation.
items.limits: Horizontal declared reservations, not automatic arbitrary-mesh bounds, 3D collision, global packing or pathfinding. Each slot tries five recipe-defined candidates against at most seven explicit reservations; pairs are checked in groups of up to six. In this garden, path reservations conservatively enclose the complete sine bend and can exclude extra space. Radius must contain the complete attached object; update it if geometry grows or is manually changed. No position fits: reject and preserve the previous scene. Candidate changes happen at edit-time or explicit film cues, not continuously during physics.
